cognate: Gk μέθυ = Ved. mádhu- (*médʰu-); Gk ἡδύς = Ved. svādú-/superl. svā́diṣṭha- (*swéh₂du-); secondary: Gk ἧμαι = Ved. √ās- (*h₁eh₁s-)
drift_or_renewal: drift of the noun: *médʰu- 'mead, honey-drink' > Ved. 'honey, sweet drink (soma)', Gk 'wine'; the epithet stays with it, though for wine Greek elsewhere uses ἡδύς with the new word οἶνος (Od. 3.51, 10.519) and μελιηδής
shared_syntax: noun + attributive 'sweet' (Gk μέθυ ἡδύ, neuter acc. object; Ved. mádhvaḥ svā́diṣṭham, partitive gen. + superlative, object of 'drink'); in the Homeric line and RV 7.32.2b also the verb 'sit' (*h₁eh₁s-) with the drink as its setting
context: Both describe the drink of a feast or offering: Indra is told to drink 'the sweetest of the madhu' (RV 8.49.4b; cf. 6.47.1 of soma 'sweet... honeyed', 10.29.6 'may the madhus be sweet for drinking'); the poets sit at the pressed soma 'like flies on madhu' (7.32.2b). Homer's formula line 'we sat feasting on endless meat and sweet μέθυ' (6x Od.) plus 'food and sweet μέθυ' (3x). ἡδύ is Homer's only epithet for μέθυ in these lines, and the pair keeps its cognate adjective even though the noun's referent has changed from honey-drink to wine, which makes it unlikely the Greek collocation was formed afresh. Caveat: 'sweet' is the natural word for honey, so the Vedic side could be ordinary language, and the 'sit' element rests on a simile in the RV.

cognate: Ved. √dhr̥ṣ- / dhr̥ṣát = Gk θαρσ-/θάρσος (*dʰers-); Ved. mánas- = Gk μένος (*ménos-)
drift_or_renewal: In the anchor line Greek has ἦτορ for the inner seat (renewal of mánas); the exact cognate μένος comes back in the support lines (μένος καὶ θάρσος). The verb is renewed: Ved. kr̥- 'make' vs. Gk δίδωμι/τίθημι/ἐνίημι/θαρσύνω.
shared_syntax: a god makes a man's *ménos 'bold': Ved. dhr̥ṣát mánaḥ kr̥ṇóṣi (participle + noun, object of 'make'; also the compound dhr̥ṣán-manas- 'bold-minded'); Gk θάρσυνον ἦτορ 'embolden the heart' (factitive verb + object) and δῶκε/θῆκε μένος καὶ θάρσος (two coordinated nouns as objects of 'give/put')
context: RV 8.62.5: 'you, Indra, make bold the mind even of the bold man'. Il. 16.242: Achilles asks Zeus to 'embolden [Patroclus'] heart in his chest'; Il. 5.2 Athena 'gave Diomedes menos and tharsos'; Od. 1.321 she 'put menos and tharsos' into Telemachus. In both traditions the same two roots name the god-given boldness of a man's inner force. Weak points: courage in the heart is common human idiom, the Greek pairing coordinates the two nouns rather than making one modify the other, and the verbs are not cognate.
phrase: *dʰr̥s- ménos 'bold mind/spirit', granted by a god

cognate: Ved. áhi- = Av. aži- (*h₁ogʷʰi-); Ved. vŕ̥ka- = Av. vəhrka- (*wl̥kʷo-)
drift_or_renewal: verb renewed: Ved. jambhaya- 'crush (with the jaws)' vs Av. jan- 'smite' and apa-duuar- 'run off' (a daevic verb); Avestan adds -ciϑra- 'of the seed of'
shared_syntax: snake and wolf coordinated, as objects of a verb of destroying or driving off, in a list of noxious beings that also holds human evildoers (Ved. rákṣāṃsi; AV stena-, yātudhāna-; Av. aṣ̌əmaōγa-, maṣ̌iiō.sāsta-)
context: RV 7.38.7: the Vājins 'crushing snake, wolf, demons' keep diseases away; AVŚ 4.3.7, an apotropaic charm: 'we crush the tiger... the thief, the snake, the sorcerer, the wolf'. Avestan Yašt (ArW 2.8-15): a litany in which the serpent-seed, the wolf-seed and the two-legged (human) evil 'run away' or are 'smitten'. In both Indic and Iranian, snake and wolf with human malefactors make up a stock class of harmful beings to be warded off in protective verse. Shared Indo-Iranian (not wider) heritage; the RV has the pair only once; snakes and wolves are obvious pests anywhere (Aristotle in this slab lists 'wolves, bears, vipers' as Crete's absent beasts), so the pairing could be independent.
phrase: Indo-Iranian *aǰʰi- + *u̯r̥ka- 'snake and wolf' in an apotropaic catalogue of the harmful

note: All 212 bundles read (every pivot is RV). Most partners were prose (Aristotle, Plato, Hippocrates, Xenophon) or OCR verse with no shared wording. Leads dropped: dā́tā vásu / dayate vásūni (B-4d11b, B-0ca51) look like δωτῆρες ἐάων, but no Greek passage in the slab has ἐάων, so the claim could not be anchored; patháḥ sātáye ~ διὰ πόντον ἀνύσσας (B-b1428) has only one Vedic attestation and a different construction; hā́rdi tviṣā́ ~ ἔσεισε καρδίαν (B-5acef) is generic; gā́m áśvam / áśvam gā́m ávyayam ~ βοῶν… οἰῶν (B-4831c, B-a4c92) are generic livestock lists; śíraḥ bibheda ~ cerebrum finditur (B-90419, B-cfd81) has incongruent contexts.
